power-bi-data-alerts.title: Set data alerts in the Power BI service
power-bi-data-alerts.notes: Data alerts tell a user when a value on a dashboard tile moves past a threshold they define. The user creates an alert rule on a tile, names it, sets the limit and chooses whether it may fire at most hourly or daily. Alerts are evaluated only when the underlying data refreshes, and they fire only when the data has changed, so an unchanged value does not repeat the message. Notifications arrive in the Power BI notification center, by email and in the mobile apps, and each one links back to the tile. Only tiles pinned from report visuals qualify, and only gauges, KPIs and cards with numeric values; card tiles built on date or time measures and tiles made with custom streaming data are excluded. Alerts can be set in My Workspace, on shared dashboards in Premium capacity, or in other workspaces with a Pro license, but not in Power BI Desktop (report-level alerting is pointed to Fabric Activator instead). Each alert is private to its creator, a person can hold up to 250 alerts, co-ownership is not supported, and alerts can be connected to Power Automate.

power-fx-user-defined-functions.title: User-defined functions, user-defined types and enhanced component properties move forward (Power Apps blog)
power-fx-user-defined-functions.notes: User-defined functions let makers wrap Power Fx logic in a named, parameterized function that can be reused across a canvas app. Earlier versions were built on named formulas, so they had to be declarative and could not change app state. The announcement describes a newer kind, behavior functions, whose body sits in curly braces and chains steps with the semicolon operator, so a function can call things like Set, Collect, Reset or Notify; an example increments a global variable and shows a notification, and a button then calls it with one argument. The author stresses that declarative style remains preferable and that behavior functions should be used only when needed. Alongside them come user-defined types, declared with the Type function, which allow functions to accept and return records and tables instead of only scalars such as Number, Text or DateTime. At the time of the post both features were experimental and had to be switched on under Settings, Updates, Experimental. The post calls this the last major update before general availability and invites feedback in the community forum. Passing untyped JSON into functions such as AddColumns is not possible; giving ParseJSON a type converts the result into a typed object.

power-usage-effectiveness.title: Power usage effectiveness (Wikipedia)
power-usage-effectiveness.notes: Power usage effectiveness measures how efficiently a data center uses energy: total facility energy divided by the energy delivered to the IT equipment. An ideal value is 1.0, meaning nothing goes to overhead such as cooling and lighting, and higher values mean more overhead; it is the inverse of data center infrastructure efficiency. The metric was developed by The Green Grid consortium, introduced in 2006 and promoted from 2007, and later published as ISO/IEC 30134-2:2016 and EN 50600-4-2:2016. Reported values include roughly 1.1 across Google sites in 2021 with the best sites under 1.06, 1.078 at a Facebook site in 2015, and 1.29 at OVH over twelve months in 2023. The article lists limits: results from different climates are not directly comparable, a busy facility can be more productive than a low-PUE one that sits idle, reducing IT load through virtualization can actually raise the ratio, measurement choices such as ignoring lighting or counting renewable generation can distort figures, and operators sometimes use it for marketing claims. Power Compute Effectiveness has been proposed as an alternative that relates provisioned compute capacity to total site electrical capacity.

powershell-pipeline.title: about_Pipelines (PowerShell documentation)
powershell-pipeline.notes: A PowerShell pipeline is a chain of commands joined by the pipeline operator, a vertical bar, where each command hands its output to the next. The commands run as a single operation from left to right, and results appear as they are produced. Unlike shells that pass text, PowerShell passes .NET objects with properties and methods, so a later stage can read a property such as file length directly, and only the final formatting step produces text. For a receiving cmdlet to accept input it needs a parameter that takes pipeline input, bound either by value (the object's type matches or converts to the parameter type) or by property name (the object has a property named like the parameter). The binding cannot be forced; if no parameter qualifies the command fails, and Get-Help with the parameter switch or Trace-Command on ParameterBinding helps diagnose it. Collections sent through the pipe are enumerated and processed one object at a time, while hashtables, dictionaries, XML nodes and strings are not enumerated automatically. Native executables can take part, and since PowerShell 7.4 raw byte streams pass through unchanged when piping between native programs.

premium-connectors.title: Types of Power Automate licenses
premium-connectors.notes: The page explains connector entitlements as part of Power Automate licensing and splits them into three groups. Standard connectors are needed to add a standard connector to a cloud flow and trigger it. Premium connectors are needed to add a premium connector to a cloud flow and trigger it. Custom connectors are needed when a service has no prebuilt connector and a maker creates one with its own triggers and actions. A paid premium user license includes all three. A free user license is shown with standard connectors only, and the premium and custom entitlements are not stated for it. Paid process licenses, including the hosted variant, include standard, premium and custom connectors; a process license assigned to a cloud flow lets that flow use premium and custom connectors regardless of the license of the person who owns or triggers it, provided the flow lives in a solution. Trial licenses allow users to try premium capabilities, though the page gives no connector detail for them. Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform licenses contain only a limited set of Power Automate capabilities, and the Power Platform Licensing Guide lists what each includes.

prep-data-for-ai.title: Prepare your data for AI (Power BI Copilot)
prep-data-for-ai.notes: Prep data for AI is a preview capability in Power BI that helps model authors make a semantic model easier for Copilot to interpret, which reduces ambiguity and improves how well answers are grounded. It works in Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service, and everything is saved to the semantic model rather than to a report. It has three parts: AI data schemas, which simplify how the model is shown to Copilot; verified answers, where an author picks a visual, chooses to set it as a verified answer and defines trigger phrases that return it; and AI instructions, which steer how Copilot responds. Instructions and schemas are kept in the linguistic schema (LSDL) and can be edited. Requirements include Q&A being enabled on the model and, in Desktop, Import, DirectQuery or composite local connections. A model can be marked Approved for Copilot in the service, but reports, dashboards and apps cannot. Limits noted: changes may take minutes to appear, approval can need up to 24 hours to spread for models with many reports, Copilot may occasionally time out when fetching the schema, and AI output is not deterministic, so identical answers are not guaranteed.

preservation-hold-library.title: Learn about retention for SharePoint and OneDrive (Microsoft Purview)
preservation-hold-library.notes: The Preservation Hold library is a hidden system library that SharePoint and OneDrive create on a site when none exists. It holds copies of content that is changed or deleted while retention applies, so users keep working normally while a compliance copy is retained. People cannot edit, delete or move these files; access is through tools such as eDiscovery. What triggers a copy depends on the rule: with a retention policy both edits and deletions create one, with a standard retention label only deletions do, with a record label editing an unlocked item copies it while editing a locked item or deleting is blocked, and with a regulatory record label both are blocked. A timer job looks at items that have sat in the library longer than 30 days, checks them against retention queries and removes those whose period has ended and that are not waiting for disposition review. It runs every seven days, so removal can take up to 37 days. For retain-and-delete settings, expired items go to the first-stage or second-stage Recycle Bin and are permanently deleted after a total of 93 days, unless another retention rule or eDiscovery hold still applies. For OneDrive accounts of departed users, retained files stay under retention.

principal-agent-problem.title: Principal-agent problem (Wikipedia)
principal-agent-problem.notes: The principal-agent problem describes the conflict that appears when one party, the agent, acts for another, the principal, but has goals that differ from the principal's. The gap matters more as interests and information diverge and as the principal loses the ability to punish the agent; the loss to the principal is called agency cost. Typical pairs are managers and shareholders, elected officials and citizens, and brokers and clients. The core difficulty is asymmetric information. Two forms are distinguished: moral hazard, where the agent's effort or actions are hidden and costly to observe so the agent may shirk or favor easily measured tasks, and adverse selection, where the agent holds private knowledge about its own type, such as its skills or costs, before a contract is signed. When one agent serves several principals the problem grows because each principal may pursue its own aims. Examples include real estate agents, landlords and tenants, and bureaucrats who know more than the ministers overseeing them.

private-branch-exchange.title: Business telephone system (Wikipedia)
private-branch-exchange.notes: A private branch exchange is a private phone network that lets people inside an organization call each other and also reach outside callers through the public switched telephone network. Because stations share a smaller pool of exchange lines, a company needs fewer external lines. The article separates several kinds. A key telephone system lets users pick outside lines manually with line buttons and needs no operator. A PBX selects outgoing lines automatically, uses an internal numbering plan and adds services such as hunt groups and call forwarding. An IP-PBX carries voice over the Internet Protocol, either on dedicated hardware or as software. A hosted PBX is run by a provider in the cloud so the customer needs no on-site equipment, and hybrid systems mix key-system and PBX features. Common functions include auto attendant, transfer, conferencing, voicemail, music on hold, direct inward dialing and automatic call distribution, with call detail records kept for accounting. Connection standards named include SIP, H.323, ISDN, DECT for cordless handsets and QSIG for linking PBXs. Early systems were operator-run manual switchboards, later replaced by electromechanical and electronic switches, and in the 1990s data networks and VoIP led to IP-PBXs.

privileged-access-workstation.title: Privileged access: Devices (Microsoft Learn)
privileged-access-workstation.notes: A privileged access workstation is a hardened device reserved for sensitive administrative work. The guidance rests on the clean source principle: if an attacker controls the device a user works from, the attacker can impersonate that user or steal credentials, which undermines the accounts, jump servers and resources behind it, so securing the device is the foundation of privileged access. Microsoft describes three device security levels. Enterprise suits general users and developers who may run any application and browse any site, and needs Defender for Endpoint and policy hardening. Specialized removes local admin rights and limits applications to those installed by an authorized administrator. The privileged level, the PAW, is for roles whose compromise would seriously affect the organization: web browsing and email are blocked by default, Credential Guard, Device Guard, App Guard and Exploit Guard are used, local disks are BitLocker encrypted, and administrators need separate devices and accounts for productivity and browsing. Principles include end-to-end security, shrinking the attack surface while keeping productivity, a hardware root of trust (TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, HVCI) and Windows Autopilot for provisioning.

process-criticality.title: How do you determine business process criticality? (Security Scientist)
process-criticality.notes: The page treats process criticality as the question of which business functions are too important to be allowed to fail, and says the answer should come from measured disruption impact rather than opinion. The main yardstick is how much damage an outage would do to operations, to reputation and to legal standing, with potential financial loss and failure of essential services as the primary concerns. It attributes to CISA a two-part approach: judge the importance of each individual process, then determine how quickly and completely it must be recovered. A simple severity scale is illustrated, from a minor internal tool whose outage goes unnoticed for hours to a primary payment gateway whose failure stops sales and revenue at once. Because systems depend on one another, a small failure can cascade, so mapping dependencies exposes hidden risk and helps set recovery criticality before an incident happens. The practical tip given is to focus on the impact of downtime rather than only on how likely an event is. The page does not discuss frequency of use as a separate factor.

process-historian.title: Operational historian (Wikipedia)
process-historian.notes: An operational historian is a time-series database built for process data from manufacturing. It is often embedded in or used next to distributed control systems and programmable logic controllers, where it adds data capture, validation, compression and aggregation. Data is organized as tags, also called points, a term that goes back to the physical tags once hung on instruments for manual recording; each stream of process values is one tag. Historians handle storage and archiving of very large volumes and also provide validation, alarm-limit monitoring, aggregation, interpolation and manual entry. Access is offered through dedicated high-speed APIs and SDKs and through OPC HDA, SQL or REST interfaces. Queries can target one tag, a time range or a number of samples, and can return raw values, the last known value, aggregates or interpolated values, optionally filtering by quality, value or count. They are rarely relational, yet many offer SQL-like interfaces with dialects adapted to time-series access. Plant engineers and operators use them mainly for supervisory control, performance monitoring, quality assurance and analysis, often through trending tools. An enterprise historian, by contrast, keeps only a subset of plant data for business functions.

product-lifecycle-management.title: Product lifecycle (Wikipedia)
product-lifecycle-management.notes: Product lifecycle management is the process of managing a product through its whole life, from early engineering and design through manufacture and service to disposal. It joins people, data, processes and business systems and serves as an information backbone for a company and its extended enterprise. The article distinguishes it from marketing-oriented lifecycle management, which deals with costs and sales; PLM covers the engineering side and is often named as one of four cornerstones of a manufacturer's IT, next to customer relationship, supply chain and enterprise resource planning systems. It centers on creating and centrally managing all product data, including graphical and textual information and bills of materials, and covers engineering changes, release status, configurations, document management and project resources. Product data management and enterprise data management systems typically hold this data. Typical phases run from concept and detailed design with simulation through tooling, manufacturing planning, production, assembly and testing, then sales, use, maintenance and disposal, and they overlap in practice. The roots are traced to American Motors Corporation in 1985, which used CAD and a central database to cut costly engineering changes.

product-process-resource.title: Recipe-based Integrated Semantic Product, Process, Resource (PPR) Digital Modelling Methodology (Procedia CIRP 17, 2014)
product-process-resource.notes: This research paper by Agyapong-Kodua, Haraszko and Nemeth, published in Procedia CIRP in 2014, describes a product, process and resource modelling methodology for manufacturing. It defines a product as a material, piece part or assembly made to be sold to a third party, which can break down into subassemblies, components and attachments such as rivets or adhesives. Processes bridge products and the manufacturing systems that make them and are organized as a hierarchy of multitasks, tasks, operations and actions. Resources cover people, machines and IT systems as well as system layouts, with ontologies for layout, equipment types and human resources. The three domains are linked by matching product and process requirements semantically against resource capabilities, using ontologies with relationships, rules and logic; candidate processes and resources can be selected during product modelling and sent to a 3D environment for simulation. The aim is to close the knowledge gap between product, process and resource, shortening design cycles and reducing errors, and to reuse knowledge through recipes, which are predefined resource solution patterns. The method was applied to a UK small manufacturer of wrenches and was supported by an EU seventh framework project.

production-routing.title: Routing (Infor LN manufacturing documentation)
production-routing.notes: In this ERP documentation a routing holds the planning data for a manufacturing method: it consists of operations, and each operation names where the work happens, which can be a work center, a specific machine at a site, or both. The sequence of operations defines how an item moves through production. A routing can be strictly sequential, or a network routing that combines ordered steps with operations running in parallel. Yield and scrap are recorded per operation, and run time and production rate can be derived from norm tables that hold standard times for two physical dimensions such as length and width. A work center groups resource units such as people and machines into one planning unit for capacity planning and is tied to an operation rate code used for standard and actual costs; machines belong to work centers and carry their own rate. Reference operations classify shop-floor work. The page lists four routing types: standard routings that can be attached to several items, item-specific routings, network routings, and order-quantity-dependent routings defined for a given quantity. Some operations require skills, which are linked to employees so assigned staff are qualified.

productized-services.title: Productized service (t2informatik Smartpedia)
productized-services.notes: A productized service turns a custom service into a standardized package in which scope, price, process and outcome are fixed in advance, so the customer buys a defined result rather than hours of effort; the core idea is selling a service the way a product is sold. The article credits Brian Casel and Dan Norris with popularizing the idea. Typical characteristics are a clearly defined target group, an outcome orientation such as an optimized landing page, a defined scope with stated inclusions and exclusions, a standardized and repeatable process (for example a briefing form) and a fixed price, ideally reflecting the value of the result rather than time spent. Providers gain focus, less dependence on daily capacity, leverage from selling the same package repeatedly and stronger branding; customers gain quick orientation, predictable expectations, lower perceived risk and easier comparison. The model tends to fail when package sales are mixed with custom work, special requests dilute the structure, automation comes before the offer is defined, scope stays vague or positioning is neglected. Building one follows six steps: define the target group, the result and the scope, document the process, set the price, then test and refine.

project-portfolio-management.title: Project portfolio management (Wikipedia)
project-portfolio-management.notes: Project portfolio management is the centralized management of the processes, methods and technologies that project managers and project management offices use to analyze and run current or proposed projects together. Recognized frameworks include those of the Project Management Institute, the UK Office of Government Commerce's Management of Portfolios and the PfM2 methodology. Its purpose is to find the best mix of resources for delivering work and to schedule activities so operational and financial goals are met within constraints set by customers, strategy and external factors; a central output is deciding which projects to fund, called project portfolio optimization. Key processes named are pipeline management (ideation, work intake and phase-gate reviews), resource management including what-if scenarios, change request management, financial management with methods such as earned value analysis, and risk management balanced across the portfolio. Enterprise PPM is a top-down approach that favors a single enterprise-wide system as one version of the truth, aiming to prioritize the right projects, spot problems early, improve governance, spread best practice and plan future resource needs.

project-server.title: Planning Project Server and Project Online for technical decision makers
project-server.notes: Project Server is Microsoft's on-premises project management platform: an organization deploys and maintains it in its own datacenter and it runs Project Web App. The article applies to Project Server Subscription Edition, 2019 and 2016. Project Online offers the same Project Web App experience but is hosted in a Microsoft datacenter, so the customer does not manage infrastructure; Microsoft recommends Project Online first unless business requirements call for on-premises Project Server. Differences covered include security, where both can use SharePoint permission mode or the more granular Project permission mode and both create seven default groups (administrators, portfolio managers, portfolio viewers, project managers, resource managers, team leads and team members), and business intelligence, where Project Server allows direct access to the content database for Excel, Reporting Services, PerformancePoint and custom OLAP cubes, while Project Online exposes data only through OData feeds and has no OLAP cubes. Hybrid reporting is possible by copying Project Online data to a data warehouse or using Power BI.

psdataverse.title: PSDataverse (GitHub repository)
psdataverse.notes: PSDataverse is a PowerShell module that exposes the Microsoft Dataverse Web API to PowerShell 7 and later. It aims for ease of use and speed and follows the conventions of native cmdlets so it combines well with other modules. It is a hybrid: part of the commands live in a compiled assembly and the rest are written in PowerShell. Features listed are a secure connection, batching and parallel execution, automatic reconnection before the token expires, strong pipeline support with several input types and responses emitted to the pipeline, automatic wait-and-retry on transient errors, respect for Dataverse throttling information, and returning the full response including headers and status code. Three sign-in methods are supported: a client ID with a secret, a client ID with a certificate in the operating system store, or an interactive device authentication flow; the first two need an application user in the Power Platform environment, and device flow with a custom app registration needs the public client flows setting enabled. The module installs from the PowerShell Gallery, or can be built from the repository.

public-key-infrastructure.title: Public key infrastructure (Wikipedia)
public-key-infrastructure.notes: A public key infrastructure is the framework of roles, policies, hardware, software and procedures for creating, managing, distributing, storing and revoking digital certificates, used where passwords alone give too little assurance of identity, such as e-commerce, online banking and confidential email. Core parts are the certificate authority, which issues and signs certificates binding a public key to a person or organization; the registration authority, which verifies applicants but under X.509 cannot sign or issue certificates; a central directory; a certificate management system; the certificate policy; and the digital certificates themselves, typically in X.509 format. In operation an identity is verified, usually by a registration authority, and the authority signs a certificate containing the public key, so anyone who trusts the authority can trust the binding, enabling encryption, integrity and authentication in either direction. Certificates can be revoked before expiry if compromised or mis-issued, and the article describes the trade-off when revocation data is unavailable: failing hard rejects the certificate and risks availability, failing soft accepts it and lets attackers bypass revocation, and browsers generally fail soft.

purview-data-security-investigations.title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations
purview-data-security-investigations.notes: Data Security Investigations is a Microsoft Purview solution that helps security teams use generative AI to analyze and respond to data security incidents, risky insiders and data breaches, finding the sensitive data an incident affected and working with partner teams to reduce the risk. Capabilities include vector-based semantic search that finds related assets even without matching keywords, plus audit search over unified audit log activity such as file access, downloads and label changes; categorization of impacted data into default, custom or AI-suggested categories by subject and risk, with standard or advanced AI options; deep content examination for hidden risks such as compromised credentials, network risks, personal data exposure and threat actor discussions; and mitigation, including soft and hard purge of items, and sharing details with internal or external stakeholders. Users are notified through the Purview notification center and email.

qaoa.title: Quantum optimization algorithms (Wikipedia, QAOA section)
qaoa.notes: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm is a quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization, where the task is to find a bit string that maximizes an objective written as a sum of Boolean clauses. It is hybrid. One defines a cost Hamiltonian whose ground state encodes the solution and a mixer Hamiltonian, a simple non-commuting sum of Pauli-X operations, and starts from an equal superposition of all basis states. The circuit alternates the cost and mixer operators, each controlled by an angle, then measures in the computational basis, and a classical optimizer updates the angles so that the expected cost improves; repeating the loop yields parameters that give a near-optimal state. The number of layers is the number of times the operator pair is applied, and more layers give more expressive power. The design draws on the quantum adiabatic theorem. The article's example finds a minimum vertex cover on a four-vertex graph with a two-layer Qiskit circuit. Variants include multi-angle QAOA and the quantum alternating operator ansatz, and MaxCut is a common application.

quality-containment.title: What automotive containment really means and how to get it right (Acuren)
quality-containment.notes: Containment is the immediate response to a defect or quality risk, meant to stop suspect parts from moving downstream while permanent fixes are worked out. The article distinguishes it from root cause analysis, which asks why the problem happened, and from rework, which tries to repair defective parts afterwards; it is a temporary safety net rather than a solution. It starts as soon as a defect or risk is identified, which means it can begin before the cause is known. Typical steps are moving questionable material into a secured holding area, inspecting and sorting inventory to separate suspect parts from acceptable ones, pausing shipments until parts are confirmed to meet requirements, checking every high-risk part instead of sampling, and keeping traceability so each affected batch is marked and monitored. The setting is automotive supply chains, where tolerances and regulatory demands are tight, safety-critical parts such as brakes and steering allow no flaws, and tiered suppliers mean one nonconformance can reach several automakers; fast containment can keep a problem from becoming a recall. The source is a service provider's blog.

quality-management-system.title: Quality management system (Wikipedia)
quality-management-system.notes: A quality management system is a collection of business processes aimed at consistently meeting customer requirements and improving satisfaction, aligned with the organization's purpose and strategy and expressed through goals, policies, processes, documented information and the resources to maintain them. The concept emerged in the Industrial Revolution, when mass production replaced craftspeople and early approaches relied on inspection; Deming later introduced statistical control and Juran a framework of quality planning, control and improvement. The term itself is credited to Ken Croucher in 1991. Common elements are quality objectives and a quality manual, organizational structure and responsibilities, data management and process control including purchasing, product quality and customer satisfaction, continuous improvement including corrective and preventive action, document control, training and supplier quality management. ISO 9001:2015 is among the most widely implemented standards and can be certified against; it requires defined processes and their interactions, measurement and analysis, management review and planned continual improvement, and includes tools such as failure mode and effects analysis. ISO 9000 and ISO 9004 are guidance only.

r-programming-language.title: R (programming language) (Wikipedia)
r-programming-language.notes: R is a programming language for statistical computing and data visualization, widely used in data mining, bioinformatics, data analysis and data science. It is free and open-source software under the GNU General Public License and became a GNU project with version 0.60 on 5 December 1997. Its core is written mainly in C, Fortran and R itself, and precompiled executables exist for Linux, macOS and Windows. Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman created it at the University of Auckland to teach introductory statistics; it was inspired by the S language, so most S programs run unchanged, and it took lexical scoping from Scheme. A binary was posted in 1993 and version 1.0 appeared on 29 February 2000. Features include an interpreted core with a command line, front ends such as RStudio and Jupyter, a multi-paradigm design with dynamic typing and native object systems S3 and S4, built-in support for statistical modelling and graphics, and a native pipe operator since version 4.1.0. The Comprehensive R Archive Network, founded in 1997, hosts source code, executables, documentation and user packages, and counted 22,390 contributed packages in mid-2025; the tidyverse is a popular package collection and Bioconductor supplies genomic tools.

raci-matrix.title: Responsibility assignment matrix (Wikipedia)
raci-matrix.notes: A RACI matrix, also called a responsibility assignment matrix or linear responsibility chart, is a project management technique that shows who does what when tasks or deliverables are completed. It is especially helpful in cross-departmental projects where responsibilities blur. Tasks sit on one axis and roles on the other, and each cell holds one participation code. Responsible marks those who carry out the work, and every task needs at least one. Accountable marks the person ultimately answerable for correct completion, who delegates, confirms prerequisites and signs off; some theories demand exactly one accountable party per task, and this role is also called the approver. Consulted marks subject-matter experts whose opinion is sought, with two-way communication. Informed marks stakeholders who are kept up to date, often at completion, with one-way communication. The article lists variants: DACI (driver, approver, contributor, informed), PARIS, RACI plus facilitation for Scrum, RASCI and similar forms that add support, CAIRO or RACIO that add omitted stakeholders, RACIQ with quality review and RACI-VSL with verifier and signatory. The model is described in the PMBOK Guide of the Project Management Institute, and the name is pronounced ray-see.

read-replica.title: Read replicas in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
read-replica.notes: In Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, a read replica is a separate read-only server instance that copies data from a primary. It is managed like a regular flexible server and billed on its own provisioned vCores and storage. Replication is asynchronous, using PostgreSQL native physical replication with streaming and replication slots by default and file-based log shipping to catch up; replicas are eventually consistent, lag usually ranges from seconds to minutes and can reach hours under heavy writes or high latency, and cross-region replicas typically lag more, so they are not suitable when up-to-the-minute accuracy is required. Main uses are offloading read-heavy work such as reporting and BI from the primary (they do not reduce write load), serving geographically distributed reads, and supporting disaster recovery. A replica can be promoted either to primary or to an independent server removed from replication, passing through states such as updating and catch-up.

reciprocal-rank-fusion.title: Relevance in hybrid search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Azure AI Search)
reciprocal-rank-fusion.notes: Reciprocal Rank Fusion is the method Azure AI Search uses to merge results when two or more queries run in parallel, such as a hybrid query combining full-text and vector search, or several vector queries. Each query yields its own ranked list. For every list a document appears in, it receives a score of one divided by its rank plus a constant k, typically 60, and the scores are summed across lists before documents are sorted by the total. BM25 scores have no upper bound while vector similarity scores sit in a narrow range, so the method ignores raw scores and uses only rank positions: a first-place BM25 hit adds about 0.0164 and a tenth-place hit about 0.0143, so a document that appears in both lists at moderate ranks can outrank one that tops only a single list. Other facts: only searchable fields are scored; each extra vector query or field adds a parallel execution; vector weights, default 1.0, multiply a list's contribution to increase or reduce its influence; the hybrid score is bounded by the number of fused queries; semantic ranking runs after fusion and reports a separate reranker score from 0 to 4; a debug setting returns subscores; and top defaults to 50 with text recall size defaulting to 1,000.

regular-expressions.title: Regular expression (Wikipedia)
regular-expressions.notes: A regular expression is a sequence of characters that defines a match pattern for text, used for find and find-and-replace operations, input validation and text processing, and also studied in formal language theory. Syntax elements include literals that match themselves, metacharacters such as the dot, which matches any character except a newline, and the caret and dollar anchors; bracket expressions like a-z or negated sets; quantifiers for zero or one, zero or more, one or more and counted ranges; alternation with a vertical bar and grouping with parentheses; and escapes such as digit, word and whitespace classes. Quantifiers are greedy by default and become lazy with a question mark. History: Stephen Kleene formalized regular languages in 1951, Ken Thompson built matching into the QED editor in 1968, the name grep comes from the ed command g/re/p, POSIX.2 standardized them in 1992 and Perl, then Philip Hazel's PCRE from 1997, added richer features. They appear in search engines, editors, sed and AWK, lexical analyzers, data validation and web scraping, and most major languages support them.

rehost.title: Migrate to Azure (Azure Migration Hub)
rehost.notes: Rehost, often called lift and shift, means moving a workload to Azure infrastructure without any code changes. The page describes it as fast and low risk and best for straightforward workloads where speed matters most; its example is moving a web application from a Windows Server virtual machine to an Azure virtual machine, which changes where the application runs but not how. It is one of eight strategies described: rehost, replatform (minimal changes to use Azure platform services, such as SQL Server to Azure SQL Managed Instance), refactor, rearchitect, retire, replace, rebuild and retain. The page states that most Azure Migration Hub migrations use rehost or replatform because keeping the workload functionally identical limits risk, that a migrated workload should meet the same KPIs, SLAs and SLOs on Azure as before, and that teams should finish the migration first and optimize or modernize afterwards. The guidance covers single-workload migrations from AWS, Google Cloud or on-premises, not full datacenter moves, region relocations or hybrid workloads on several clouds.

released-product.title: Product information management overview (Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management)
released-product.notes: In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management a released product is a product that has been released to a specific legal entity. Products are defined centrally, with a product number, name and description and related data such as type, dimensions, categories, attributes, images, units of measure and translations, and then released to one or many legal entities, in bulk if wanted. Because each legal entity may need its own properties and attributes, a Released product maintenance workspace lets teams monitor and complete recently released products per legal entity or suborganization; it shows open product change cases and a list of recently released products with validation status, which can reveal unfinished legal entity configuration, and time fences in days can be set for recently released and stopped released products. Creating a released product manually creates a new product and releases it to the current legal entity in one step. Product data can be created in the application or imported from PLM, PDM or PIM systems, with one instance acting as master when there are several, and definitions can be exported to Dataverse for apps such as Dynamics 365 Sales.

remaining-useful-life.title: Prognostics / Remaining useful life (Wikipedia)
remaining-useful-life.notes: The article on prognostics defines the field as predicting when a system or component will stop performing its intended function; the predicted time to that point is the remaining useful life, which supports contingency planning. It is closely tied to condition-based maintenance and is often called prognostics and health management. Estimation approaches are data-driven (pattern recognition, machine learning and stochastic models such as autoregressive models and neural networks, which deploy quickly but need large datasets, and run-to-failure data is costly), model-based or physics-based (equations at material or system level, such as crack-growth models, which can be precise but narrow and labor intensive), and hybrid combinations that fuse both to reduce uncertainty. Uncertainty comes from imprecise parameters, simplified nominal models, variable degradation trends, unpredictable future operating conditions and failure thresholds that may shift; Kalman and particle filters help manage it, and performance is judged with metrics such as prognostic horizon, alpha-lambda accuracy, relative accuracy and convergence. Accuracy matters most near failure, when little time remains for action.

remote-desktop-protocol.title: Remote Desktop Protocol (Wikipedia)
remote-desktop-protocol.notes: The Remote Desktop Protocol is a proprietary Microsoft protocol that gives a user a graphical interface to another computer over a network: client software runs on one machine and server software on the other. Clients exist for Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS and Android, while servers are built into Windows server and professional editions but not home editions. By default the server listens on TCP and UDP port 3389. Versions began with RDP 4.0 in Windows NT 4.0 Terminal Server Edition, and later releases added printer support, 24-bit color and sound, TLS encryption, Network Level Authentication (RDP 6.0), RemoteFX GPU virtualization (7.1), adaptive graphics and TLS 1.2 (8.0), restricted admin mode (8.1) and H.264 compression with 32-bit color (10.0). Features include clipboard, audio, file system and printer redirection, publishing individual programs and scripting through WMI. The article lists a history of security problems: a default man-in-the-middle weakness in RDP 5.2, the critical MS12-020 flaw in 2012, the CredSSP flaw CVE-2018-0886 and the wormable BlueKeep flaw CVE-2019-0708 patched in 2019, which also covered end-of-life Windows XP.

report-definition-language.title: Report Definition Language (SSRS)
report-definition-language.notes: Report Definition Language is the XML representation of a SQL Server Reporting Services report definition. A report definition holds the information needed to retrieve data and lay out a report, including parameters, data sources, datasets and the layout itself. Because RDL is plain XML, any protocol or programming interface that can handle XML can read or write it, and tools can generate it with System.Xml, XmlTextWriter or LINQ to XML; developers can also call code assemblies from report definition files to customize values, styles and formatting. The language is described by an XML Schema Definition, ReportDefinition.xsd, which fixes where elements may occur, their data types and how often they may appear; a complex type is by convention named after its element with the suffix Type, so ReportParameters uses ReportParametersType. The schema ships in the product's Extras folder and can also be fetched from a report server. RDL defines typed values such as Boolean, DateTime, Integer, Float, String, Size and Enum, with mappings from common language runtime types, and the largest Size value is 160 inches. Standard reports are stored in files with the rdl extension and client-side reports use rdlc, both with the text/xml media type. The page does not mention Power BI.

reprompt-attack.title: Reprompt: a single-click Microsoft Copilot attack (Varonis Threat Labs)
reprompt-attack.notes: Varonis Threat Labs disclosed Reprompt, a data-exfiltration attack first found in Microsoft Copilot Personal that needs only one click on a legitimate Microsoft link, with no plugins, connectors or further prompts from the user. It combines three techniques. Parameter-to-prompt injection abuses the q URL parameter, which pre-fills and automatically runs a prompt when the page loads. The double-request technique exploits the fact that Copilot's leak safeguards applied only to the first request, so the attacker tells it to perform each action twice. The chain-request technique has the attacker's server send follow-up instructions based on Copilot's previous answers, creating a continuous hidden exchange. After the click, Copilot runs the hidden prompt inside the victim's active session even if the chat is closed, and the server requests details such as time, location, user information and a summary of the last conversation, which Copilot sends to attacker-controlled URLs piece by piece. Because the real commands come from the server, inspecting the initial link reveals little and client-side monitoring may miss the leak. Varonis says Microsoft patched the issue and that Microsoft 365 Copilot enterprise customers were not affected.

request-for-quotation.title: Request for quotation (Wikipedia)
request-for-quotation.notes: A request for quotation is a business process in which a company or public body asks suppliers to submit price quotes for specified products or services, and the term is generally treated as equivalent to a call for bids or invitation for bid. A quote usually covers more than unit price; buyers may also ask about payment terms, quality levels per item or contract length. Because suppliers must price the same thing, requests carry detailed specifications, which make quotes more accurate and easier to compare and may serve as legally binding documentation. Suppliers must return bids by a fixed date and time, buyers may hold clarification talks, and bidding can run through several rounds; procurement teams then compare quotes and negotiate or run an e-auction such as a reverse auction, with the goal of establishing fair market value and saving money. Government agencies often publish requests on official or vendor-run sites, and the whole process can be conducted online. The article says the method suits products and services that are as standardized and commoditized as possible, and notes that organizations sometimes use it where a request for tender or request for information would fit better.

resource-drift.title: Detect and manage drift with Terraform (HashiCorp tutorial)
resource-drift.notes: In the Terraform tutorial, resource drift is a mismatch between real infrastructure and the Terraform state, usually caused by someone changing a resource manually instead of through Terraform. The tutorial advises against manual changes to managed resources because the mismatch can lead Terraform to destroy or recreate things on its next run. By default Terraform compares state with real infrastructure during plan and apply. To check for drift without acting, run plan with the refresh-only option, which lists objects changed outside Terraform and shows how the state would change; the tutorial prefers this over the older refresh subcommand, which overwrites state without displaying the updates, and the flag arrived in Terraform 0.15.4. Remediation has four steps: record the real state with apply in refresh-only mode, which updates state without touching infrastructure; update the configuration to include what was created by hand; import unmanaged resources with terraform import (configuration-driven import is available from Terraform 1.5); then run a normal apply so infrastructure and configuration agree.

retry-pattern.title: Retry pattern (Azure Architecture Center)
retry-pattern.notes: The retry pattern deals with transient faults, the short-lived failures that cloud applications meet when calling remote services: momentary connectivity loss, a service that is briefly unavailable, or timeouts while a service is busy. These faults usually fix themselves, so repeating a failed request after a suitable delay often succeeds. The solution is to wrap remote calls in a retry mechanism that attempts a limited number of times and then treats the failure as an exception. The page describes three responses: cancel when the fault is not transient or unlikely to clear, retry immediately for rare one-off faults such as a corrupted packet, and retry after a delay for common busy or connectivity faults, with delays growing incrementally or exponentially up to a maximum count. Intervals should spread out requests from many application instances, which is the purpose of jitter, although the page does not use that word.

return-on-security-investment.title: What is ROSI: return on security investment (Check Point)
return-on-security-investment.notes: Return on security investment applies return-on-investment logic to cybersecurity spending so security leaders can show that past investments paid off and justify future ones. The page gives the formula as the benefit of the investment minus its cost, divided by its cost. Costs are usually easy to determine while benefits are harder, so the page estimates benefit as the reduction in annual loss expectancy. That figure is the annual rate of occurrence multiplied by single loss expectancy: the first is how often an incident is expected per year, for example a 20 percent yearly chance of a denial-of-service attack equals 0.2, and the second is the total cost of one incident, including direct costs such as remediation and lost productivity and indirect costs such as lost sales. An investment's benefit comes from lowering the frequency of incidents, their impact, or both. Suggested uses are running a risk assessment to find where unmanaged risk is greatest, comparing proposed solutions by their potential ROSI, favoring prevention over detection and response, and raising security operations efficiency by cutting manual work and centralizing visibility. It is published by a security vendor.

ring-based-deployment.title: Phase rollout with rings (Azure DevOps)
ring-based-deployment.notes: Ring-based deployment is a strategy for releasing an application to production in stages so exposure grows gradually and problems are found before everyone is affected. In this Azure Pipelines guidance, a ring is a group of production instances: each production ring represents several instances of the same web application deployed to different geographic locations, rather than a separate codebase. The example classic release pipeline deploys first to a dev stage, then to two parallel QA stages, then to Prod ring 1 only after validation succeeds in both QA stages, and finally to Prod ring 2 once the application is in ring 1. Each step widens exposure only after the previous one passed, which the page says enables gradual rollouts, controlled validation and reduced risk. Validation happens through pre-deployment approvals, where approvers must sign off before a stage's deployment job starts, post-deployment approvals before the pipeline moves on, detailed deployment logs per step, and redeployment of the same release to a stage if it fails.

riskiq.title: RiskIQ (Wikipedia)
riskiq.notes: RiskIQ was a cybersecurity company based in San Francisco that sold cloud-based software-as-a-service tools for detecting online threats such as phishing, fraud and malware. It was co-founded in 2009 by Elias Manousos, Chris Kiernan and David Pon, although the article is inconsistent about the first founder's given name. Summit Partners provided a 10 million dollar Series A in February 2013 and Battery Ventures a 25 million dollar Series B in May 2014, and RiskIQ was a member of the Cloud Security Alliance. Its services included monitoring advertising networks for malicious advertising and spyware, and mobile app security; in 2018 Standard Bank used its software to automate analysis of brand infringement, cybercrime and web-based attacks against its digital presence. Microsoft acquired RiskIQ in July 2021 for more than 500 million dollars, and the company now operates as a Microsoft subsidiary. The article itself warns of some internal inconsistencies, including the founder name and certain citation retrieval dates, so details beyond the headline facts should be checked against other sources.

rot-data.title: What is ROT data? A 6-step guide to automating data minimization (Veeam)
rot-data.notes: ROT stands for redundant, obsolete and trivial data: content with no realistic future business or legal purpose that still consumes storage, permissions and attention. It builds up across public and private clouds, on-premises systems and SaaS platforms, and the article estimates that shadow data, much of it ROT, may be 40 to 90 percent of enterprise data. Redundant data means duplicate or near-duplicate copies, such as repeated report exports; obsolete data once served a purpose, like records of former employees or superseded documentation; trivial data never had business relevance, like personal files. Risks include a larger attack surface because forgotten repositories are unmonitored copies of sensitive data, degraded AI output because systems that retrieve outdated documents can give confident but wrong answers, higher costs because redundant copies are also replicated and backed up, and compliance exposure when personal data is kept beyond required periods under rules such as GDPR and CPRA. The source is a vendor blog.

salami-slicing-attack.title: Salami slicing (Wikipedia)
salami-slicing-attack.notes: A salami attack, or salami slicing, is a fraud scheme in which a large sum is accumulated through repeated transfers of imperceptibly small amounts, and more broadly any case where many small actions add up to a result that would be hard or illegal to achieve in one step. In computerized banking it typically means diverting tiny sums, often fractions left over from rounding, into a beneficiary's account; transactions calculated to the smallest currency unit leave unaccounted fractions that can be redirected, and the same idea underlies some automatic-savings apps. Cases cited include four men charged in Los Angeles in 1998 over chips in gasoline pumps that slightly overstated the quantity pumped, so customers were billed for more fuel than their tanks could hold; a man arrested in 2008 for creating 58,000 accounts to collect verification deposits of a few cents each from online brokerages; and coin thefts from fare boxes in Edmonton and Buffalo over many years, which are not computing-based but follow the same incremental pattern. The scheme relies on scale and on amounts too small for victims to notice.

sales-forecasting.title: Overview of sales forecasting (Dynamics 365 Sales)
sales-forecasting.notes: Sales forecasting in Dynamics 365 Sales gives sellers, managers and leadership a shared, near real-time view of expected revenue. It combines pipeline activity, forecast categories, quotas and hierarchy rollups, and the page presents it as a planning tool rather than a reporting artifact: comparing committed revenue, best-case opportunities and gaps to target lets teams act earlier in the sales cycle. A forecast grid is organized by team hierarchy, and forecast configuration defines the grid columns, the forecast type, the hierarchy and access permissions; the page mentions categories such as committed and best case but does not define the full set or how each is calculated. Sellers use it to track performance against quota and spot pipeline risk, managers to monitor and coach, directors to anticipate trends and move resources, and leadership to adjust strategy. Teams can start at once with the out-of-the-box forecast covering the current month or activate a sample forecast, while forecast owners or admins configure the real one in a seven-step process. Managers can adjust values for factors not yet in the system, such as a verbal customer commitment, and owners can share forecasts with others in the hierarchy.

sales-lead.title: Qualify and convert a lead to an opportunity (Dynamics 365 Sales)
sales-lead.notes: In Dynamics 365 Sales a lead is an unvetted prospect, while an opportunity is a validated deal the team actively works to close. Qualifying a lead turns it into an opportunity by confirming it is a genuine prospect, associating it with an account and contact, and creating the opportunity record. A seller opens the lead, optionally links an existing account and contact, adds details such as purchase time frame and estimated budget and selects Qualify; the lead status becomes Qualified and the lead moves to the Closed Leads view, and the business process flow advances only if an opportunity is created. How records are created depends on admin configuration: the new experience can create accounts, contacts and opportunities automatically, manually or in a mix, can allow up to five opportunities per lead and can add an AI-generated lead summary to timelines, while the legacy experience creates records automatically or through a selection dialog. Several leads can be qualified at once from the Leads grid. If a lead will not become an opportunity it can be disqualified, which keeps an audit trail and allows later reactivation with notes and attachments, but only when no opportunity is associated; deleting removes them permanently.

sales-opportunity.title: Manage opportunities (Dynamics 365 Sales)
sales-opportunity.notes: In Dynamics 365 Sales an opportunity represents a sales deal that is created when a lead is ready to buy, and sellers use it to track a potential sale until it is won or lost. According to the page an opportunity lets users forecast sales revenue, set a potential close date and assign a probability that the sale will happen; the page does not list further fields or describe stages. Administrators define the seller experience: they can configure the Sales Opportunity Agent, which gives AI-generated insights and recommendations and is labeled preview for sellers, set up predictive opportunity scoring, and customize the Opportunity Close form to capture details at closing. Sellers and sales managers create opportunities, review agent research insights, use predictive scores to prioritize deals and improve conversion, and work either from the pipeline view, which visualizes the sales pipeline with metrics, or from the focused view, which manages sales records and related activities in one place and can be set as the default by admins. Opportunities are closed as won or lost. The page footer shows an update date in April 2026.

sap-successfactors.title: SAP SuccessFactors (Wikipedia)
sap-successfactors.notes: SAP SuccessFactors is a provider of cloud-based human capital management software delivered as software as a service, headquartered in South San Francisco and a subsidiary of the German software company SAP. It was founded in 2001 in California, with the article naming Lars Dalgaard, and in the infobox also Aaron Au, as founders. It listed on NASDAQ in November 2007 under the symbol SFSF and moved to the NYSE and the Frankfurt exchange in July 2008. Before the SAP deal it bought several companies: Infohrm, an Australian HR analytics business, and CubeTree, a social software firm, in 2010; YouCalc, a Danish SaaS firm; Plateau, a learning management developer, and Jambok, a social learning platform, in 2011; and Jobs2Web, bought for 110 million dollars in cash in December 2011. SAP announced on 3 December 2011 that it would acquire all outstanding shares, and the acquisition closed on 16 February 2012, after which the company was renamed SAP SuccessFactors. In October 2013 the platform was opened through SAP Cloud Platform, and partner applications such as Accenture's were shown at SAPPHIRE 2014. In January 2022 SAP reported 12,000 customers and 191 million users in more than 200 countries. The article does not describe individual product modules.

sap.title: SAP (Wikipedia)
sap.notes: SAP SE is a German multinational software company headquartered in Walldorf, Baden-Wuerttemberg, which describes itself as the world's largest vendor of enterprise software. It operates in 78 countries with roughly 110,000 employees and belongs to the DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 indices. Five former IBM engineers, Dietmar Hopp, Hans-Werner Hector, Hasso Plattner, Klaus Tschira and Claus Wellenreuther, left IBM in 1972 and founded System Analysis and Program Development; their first client was the German unit of Imperial Chemical Industries, for which they wrote payroll and accounting programs, and a financial accounting product in 1973 became the basis of SAP R/1. Its core offering is enterprise resource planning software, which evolved through R/2 in 1979, the client-server R/3 in 1992, ERP Central Component from 2004 with ECC 6.0 in 2006, and S/4HANA from 2015, built on the HANA in-memory database. SAP also sells human capital management, customer relationship management, supply chain, product lifecycle and procurement software, plus the Business Technology Platform, and bought SuccessFactors, Ariba and Concur between 2012 and 2014. It became a European Company (SE) in 2014.

schedule-board.title: Use the schedule board in Field Service (Dynamics 365)
schedule-board.notes: The schedule board in Dynamics 365 Field Service gives dispatchers an overview of resource availability and bookings and lets them schedule, reassign and manage bookings for work orders and other requirements. It has an actions area at the top, a resource list and a requirement pane that shows unscheduled requirements. Three views exist: Gantt, showing activity over time; list, with expandable resources and time granularity; and map, showing resources, requirements and routes for one day. Time scales run from hourly to monthly, and a legend explains status, priority, timeline and travel-time colors. Dispatchers create a booking with Book, drag bookings to reschedule, move them to another day through a menu, or select a requirement and use Find availability to open the schedule assistant, which lists matching available resources. A details panel shows booking, resource or requirement information. Right-clicking a resource shows its card with skills and roles or gives driving directions, and booking alerts can be created and viewed. The board refreshes manually or automatically when relevant bookings change, though schedule assistant availabilities do not refresh with it, and a link can be copied to share a board with its settings.

scope-1-2-3-emissions.title: Carbon accounting (Wikipedia)
scope-1-2-3-emissions.notes: Within the article on carbon accounting, the three scopes are the categories of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Scope 1 means direct emissions from sources within an organization's boundary, such as fuel combustion, company vehicles and fugitive emissions. Scope 2 means indirect emissions from purchased electricity, heat, cooling or steam. Scope 3 covers all other indirect emissions across the value chain, including those from suppliers, product use and transport of goods, and the protocol defines 15 Scope 3 categories, not all of which apply to every organization. The protocol was developed by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development, starting work in 1998 with a first version in September 2001, and the article calls it a comprehensive, global, standardized framework and the most common set of standards in greenhouse gas accounting, built on principles of relevance, completeness, consistency, transparency and accuracy. Most companies reporting to CDP use it or a protocol derived from it.

search-engine-optimization.title: Search engine optimization (Wikipedia)
search-engine-optimization.notes: Search engine optimization is the practice of improving how websites and pages appear in search engine results, aiming at unpaid or organic traffic rather than paid advertising. It applies to web, image, video, news, academic and vertical search and to AI-assisted search, usually as part of a wider digital marketing strategy, with the goal of reaching people actively looking for information, products or services. Search engines discover and index pages with automated crawlers, and sites can guide this with robots.txt, noindex tags and XML sitemaps submitted through tools such as Google Search Console. Ranking depends on on-page factors such as keywords, titles, meta descriptions, headings and site structure, and off-page factors such as inbound links; Google's PageRank, developed by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998, measures prominence largely through the quantity and quality of links. Other practices include canonicalizing duplicate URLs, keeping content fresh and mobile-first indexing, which Google has applied since 2016. White hat SEO follows search engine guidelines and aims for lasting results, while black hat uses deceptive tactics such as hidden text and risks penalties.

secure-key-release.title: Secure Key Release with Azure Key Vault and Azure Confidential Computing
secure-key-release.notes: Secure key release releases an HSM-protected key from Azure Key Vault to an attested trusted execution environment, such as an SGX enclave, an AMD SEV-SNP confidential VM or a confidential container. It adds an access layer to data encryption and decryption keys so that only a specific application running in a known configuration can obtain the key material. It works with Azure Key Vault Premium and Managed HSM. Release decisions rest only on claims in Microsoft Azure Attestation tokens: the application performs remote attestation, Azure Attestation issues a signed token, and Key Vault checks its claims against the release policy that was attached when the exportable key was created. The policy is JSON with a top-level list of alternatives, each naming an attestation authority and a set of claims that must match, for example an attestation type of sevsnpvm and a compliance status of azure-compliant-cvm. The Premium workflow is to create a vault with the premium SKU, write the policy, create an exportable RSA-HSM key with the policy, and have the environment attest and request the release. Trusted Launch VMs can also produce tokens, so policies can gate on secure boot or PCR claims, but a confidential offering is needed to protect keys from the host in memory.

security-compute-unit.title: Manage usage of Security Compute Units (Security Copilot)
security-compute-unit.notes: Security Compute Units measure how much capacity Microsoft Security Copilot consumes. This page covers managing that usage rather than defining the unit, and points to another article for definitions and capacity models. Provisioned SCUs form the reserved baseline, and overage units cover use beyond it; owners set both under Owner settings. A usage monitoring dashboard shows up to 90 days of data per capacity, with columns such as session ID, date, units used, who initiated it, category (prompt, promptbook, agent or primitive), manual or automated type, Copilot experience, plugin and status, and the data can be exported to Excel. Analysts get a warning as usage nears the provisioned limit, and at 100 percent new prompts are blocked until more capacity is available, which the page says happens within the next hour; owners can prevent that by raising SCUs or limiting prompts. Azure capacity owners or contributors can change units in the Azure portal or Security Copilot portal, the latter also requiring Security Copilot owner status, and changes take effect within 30 minutes, with the estimated monthly cost assuming capacity runs 24 hours a day. The page gives no per-unit prices and no Microsoft 365 E5 allotment.

self-service-portal.title: Overview of knowledge management (Dynamics 365 Customer Service)
self-service-portal.notes: Knowledge management in Dynamics 365 Customer Service lets an organization author, categorize, deliver, analyze and share information through a knowledge base, so service representatives resolve issues faster and customers can solve problems themselves. When a portal includes the knowledge base it becomes a customer self-service portal: users in any role can select Knowledge Base and search articles with simple queries, which reduces support tickets and can raise satisfaction, and administrators can also connect a Copilot agent to answer simple questions and resolve simple issues so representatives can focus on complex cases. Authors can create major and minor versions to track changes, translate articles into several languages, publish as soon as they are approved or on a schedule, set expiration dates, have reviewers check accuracy and use templates with prepopulated fields for consistent branding and structure. Representatives search through smart assist or the knowledge search pane in the Copilot Service workspace, and administrators can federate searches across external sources such as site map-based enterprise websites ingested into Dataverse.

semantic-link.title: What is semantic link? (Microsoft Fabric)
semantic-link.notes: Semantic link connects Power BI semantic models, formerly called datasets, to the Data Science workload in Microsoft Fabric and is supported only in Fabric. Its goals are to ease data connectivity, carry semantic information into data science work and integrate with familiar tools such as notebooks. It moves data and its business meaning out of Power BI so data scientists can use semantic models for statistical analysis and machine learning, store results in OneLake with Apache Spark and bring them back into Power BI through Direct Lake. A semantic model gives a single tabular object model with reliable definitions such as Power BI measures, and semantic information such as data categories, table relationships and hierarchies travels with the data, which supports lineage and reduces errors. Two connectivity options exist: SemPy, a Python library that works with the pandas ecosystem, and a Spark native connector for PySpark, Spark SQL, R and Scala. The core data structure is FabricDataFrame, a subclass of the pandas DataFrame that keeps all pandas operations while adding semantic and lineage metadata, semantic functions and an add-measure method.

server-message-block.title: Server Message Block (Wikipedia)
server-message-block.notes: Server Message Block is a communication protocol for sharing files, printers, serial ports and other resources between network nodes. On Windows it runs through the Server service, which offers shared resources, and the Workstation service, which reaches resources on other computers; it uses NTLM or Kerberos for authentication, offers authenticated inter-process communication over named pipes, and its server component uses TCP port 445. IBM's Barry Feigenbaum created it in 1983, Microsoft and 3Com added it to LAN Manager in 1987, and the 1996 CIFS release was a lightly modified SMB 1.0. SMB 1.0 is chatty and limited to 64K blocks, performs poorly over wide-area links, was deprecated in 2013 and is no longer installed by default in newer Windows. SMB 2.0 in 2006 cut the command set from over a hundred to nineteen and added pipelining; SMB 3.0 in Windows 8 added SMB Direct over RDMA, multichannel and transparent failover; SMB 3.1.1 added stronger integrity checks and AES-128 GCM alongside CCM. Message signing protects against tampering and man-in-the-middle attacks, and SMB 3.0 introduced end-to-end encryption.

service-mesh.title: Service mesh (Wikipedia)
service-mesh.notes: A service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer that handles communication between services or microservices, typically using proxies so this work does not have to be built into each application. The article describes the pattern as pairing each service with its own network proxy, and those paired proxies carry out the mesh's work for their service; it does not use the term sidecar itself. The architecture has two parts. The data plane consists of the proxies, which intercept and process calls between services. The control plane is the set of management processes, described as the brain of the mesh, which coordinates proxy behavior and provides APIs that operations staff use to manipulate and observe the whole network. Benefits listed are observability into service communications, secure connections and automated retries and backoff for failed requests. Named implementations include Istio, Cilium, Linkerd, Consul, AWS App Mesh, Kuma, Traefik Mesh and Greymatter.io, and many use the Envoy proxy in the data plane. The article does not cover mutual TLS or policy enforcement in any detail, so those aspects should be taken from vendor documentation of a specific mesh.

shadow-automation.title: Shadow automation (Webiano knowledge base)
shadow-automation.notes: The article defines shadow automation as workflows, bots, scripts and integrations that employees build and run outside an organization's approved governance, without registration, security review or ongoing oversight, and calls it a specific form of shadow IT. Where shadow IT is usually an unapproved application, shadow automation is an unapproved process that moves data and takes actions automatically, so the concern is logic running unmonitored that can change business outcomes. It typically appears when building automation is faster than getting it approved, through low-code flows, spreadsheet macros, desktop scripts, consumer integration services, RPA bots and AI assistants with tool access. Rather than banning automation, the article recommends a cycle of discover, triage, adopt, retire and prevent, and cites a bank that found over 300 personal flows, about a fifth active, some copying loan data to personal storage.

shared-access-signature.title: Control access to IoT Hub with shared access signatures
shared-access-signature.notes: IoT Hub uses shared access signature tokens to authenticate and authorize both devices and back-end services. A token is time-bounded and signed with a key, either a shared access policy key or a device's symmetric key, and the key itself is never sent over the wire. Shared access policies grant hub-level permissions, with defaults such as iothubowner for everything, service for service connect, device for device connect and registry read or read-write. Service tokens are signed with a policy key, scoped to the hub and carry the policy name in the skn field. Device tokens come in two forms: signed with a device's symmetric key, with the resource scoped to that device and no policy name, where each device holds two such keys granting device-connect rights for itself only; or signed with the device policy by a protocol gateway or token service, scoped to one device or to all devices. A token is built from the lowercase URL-encoded resource URI (sr), an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the URI and expiry computed with the base64-decoded key (sig), the expiry in seconds since the Unix epoch (se) and optionally the policy name.

sharepoint-content-types.title: What is a content type? (Microsoft 365 PnP community docs)
sharepoint-content-types.notes: The article describes a SharePoint content type as a business object, comparable to the items people handle at a desk, rather than a mere label for a kind of content. SharePoint ships generic types such as Item and Document and a few matching common business items such as Event; organizations create custom types by inheriting from one of these and extending it to represent what they actually manage. Metadata columns added to a content type capture details about each item. The example is a mortgage document that might record a signing date, lender, contact information and amount, and later an originator, servicing company and due date, and the author advises collecting only metadata that supports the intended use cases. Metadata makes functions possible: a view listing mortgages due in the next 30 days works only when documents carry the correct content type and a populated due date. The page presents structured metadata as a way for people to do their jobs better. A content type can be defined in an individual site, in the content type hub or through site scripts, and the choice depends on scope: a benefits description may suit one HR site, while a contract may be useful across the whole tenant. The article does not use the term site columns.
